title: Count and cut posts the way the product spec counts

blocks.text: The composer under a post's text box shows `used/limit`, and the preview cuts a post that is over the limit. The product spec counts one character per Unicode code point, so 🎉 is one character. Users report that a post with a few emoji shows a count higher than the characters they typed, and that some previews end in a `?` box where an emoji was cut.

items: `length(post)`: the post's length by the spec's count;
`truncate(post, max)`: the first `max` characters of the post, by the same count.

blocks.text: About four lines in total. The tests use emoji that are each one code point; flags and emoji with skin tones, which are several, are out of scope.

cases.says: the counter shows the length of a plain-text post against the limit
a plain post over the limit is cut to the limit, and a short one is left alone
an emoji outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts as one character, so a post exactly at the limit is not cut
cutting a post keeps whole emoji and never leaves half of one

origin.section: String.chars() Streams UTF-16 Units, Not Characters

concepts: String.chars() streams UTF-16 units, so a supplementary character counts twice and a cut can split it; codePoints() streams code points.
